brief: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has turned more hawkish, telling Jackson Hole the Fed must see inflation moving to its objective clearly and at sufficient speed, and warning hikes are likely if it does not improve at a satisfactory speed. Strong August data reinforced this: nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 versus a 55,000 consensus with a further 55,000 in upward revisions, and PCE inflation ran 3.7% year over year in July, both above expectations. Market-implied odds of a September hike rose to around 60%. UBS now expects two 25bp hikes, in September and December, taking the fed funds range to 4.00-4.25%. UBS argues this hawkish shift does not imply a worse investment outlook: the same strength in employment, AI capital spending and earnings driving the hawkishness also supports growth, so the growth hit from two hikes should be modest and growth stays near trend. UBS therefore retains a constructive outlook, favoring diversified equities despite possible short-term volatility from higher yields, and expects higher yields to narrow short-duration bonds' advantage over cash while opening entry points in medium- to long-maturity high-quality bonds, to be assessed carefully.
